# Pairwise Skill Comparison

Compare two skills across:

- identity, users, triggers, exclusions, outputs;
- workflow, state, failure, recovery, and authority;
- tools, permissions, dependencies, and external effects;
- prompts, references, scripts, assets, and context loading;
- routing, behavior, security, performance, and portability evals;
- provenance, license, ownership, version, lifecycle, and consumers.

Use `shared`, `A-only`, `B-only`, `conflicting`, and `unknown` classifications. Attribute every strength and weakness to evidence or a stated rubric. A shorter file, more scripts, or more tests is not automatically better.

Recommend `improve-A`, `improve-B`, `improve-both`, `keep`, `compose`, or `assess-refactor`. Actual mutation belongs to `skill-optimizer` or `skill-refactor`.
